chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

When a man divorces his wife, they inherit from one another as long as she remains in the waiting period. But when he divorces her with the third divorce, he has no right of return to her, and there is no inheritance between them.

key_terms.التَّطْلِيقَةَ الثَّالِثَةَ: the third divorce, after which the marriage is no longer revocable
key_terms.الرَّجْعَةُ: the husband's right to take back his wife during a revocable divorce
key_terms.الْعِدَّةِ: the waiting period a divorced woman observes before the divorce is fully concluded

ai.seo_question: Do divorced spouses still inherit from each other during the 'iddah in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on inheritance between a husband and wife after divorce. During the wife's 'iddah following a revocable divorce, mutual inheritance remains in effect; but after the third divorce, the husband no longer has the right of الرجعة, and inheritance between them ceases.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5666 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said: "

When a man divorces his wife, they inherit from one another as long as she is in her waiting period (iddah). However, if he divorces her for the third time, he has no right to take her back, and there is no inheritance between them."
